clue.text: Athlete filmed in front of golf club

parts.note: a scene that has been filmed has been shot
a putter is the golf club used on the green

explanation.surface: A sportsman appears on camera standing beside a piece of golf equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in front of' simply puts the first piece before the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A shot-putter is a field-event competitor who hurls a heavy metal ball.

clue.text: Dismissal in place of retirement

definitions.meaning: first meaning: being fired from a job
second meaning: slang for bed, where one retires at night

explanation.walkthrough: 'Retirement' suggests leaving work for good, which chimes with dismissal; here it means going to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is informal both for being fired and for bed, the spot where you turn in for the night.

clue.text: Offer too much in old part of speech I had shortened

parts.note: a verb is one of the parts of speech
I had shortened to a contraction is I'd, written without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: An auction-room bidder overpays while making a clipped, old-fashioned remark.
explanation.definitionFit: To overbid is to bid more than something is worth, for instance at an auction or in bridge.

clue.text: Soldier and other ranks embracing cult? It's none of the state's business

definitions.text: It's none of the state's business

indicators.note: embracing means holding round, so the soldier and other ranks are wrapped around the cult

parts.note: a private is a soldier of the lowest rank
OR is the military abbreviation for other ranks
a sect is a religious group, a cult

explanation.surface: An army unit is accused of harbouring a cult, prompting the question whether the government should get involved.
explanation.walkthrough: The cult sits between the soldier and the other ranks.
explanation.definitionFit: The private sector is the part of the economy run by private firms, not by government.

clue.text: Cuts some slack, so to speak, for powerful people

indicators.note: so to speak signals that the answer is said aloud like the phrase before it

parts.note: taking up some of the slack in a rope tightens it

explanation.surface: Someone is being lenient toward the mighty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cuts some slack' reads as the idiom for being lenient, but literally it means reducing slack, which tightens; TIGHTENS said aloud gives TITANS.
explanation.definitionFit: Titans were giant gods in Greek myth, so the word is used for people of great power or influence.

clue.text: Work of man of letters included in book collection

definitions.text: Work of man of letters included in book collection

parts.words: Work of man of letters included in book collection
parts.note: the letters of St Paul and others are writings gathered into the New Testament, part of the Bible, a collection of books

explanation.surface: A writer's output appears in an anthology.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man of letters' usually means a literary figure; here it is a man who wrote letters, such as St Paul, whose letters form part of the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: Epistles are formal letters, especially the apostolic letters forming books of the New Testament.

clue.text: For instance, one area that covers much of the planet

definitions.text: For instance, one area that covers much of the planet

parts.note: as, in the sense 'such as', introduces an example
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An example is given of a region large enough to take up a good part of the globe.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue both builds the word and describes it: the largest continent is one such region.
explanation.definitionFit: Asia is the largest continent, covering about a third of the Earth's land.

clue.text: Sink warship north of port, perhaps

indicators.note: in a down clue, north of means written above, so this piece comes first

parts.note: a sub, short for submarine, is a warship
port is one side of a ship, an example of a side

explanation.surface: A naval vessel goes down near the harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' suggests a harbour, but it is the left side of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: To subside is to sink or settle lower, as ground or floodwater does.

clue.text: It's completely, or only partly, crucial to get here

indicators.note: only partly means only a portion of the words that follow is used, so the answer lies inside them

explanation.surface: Someone stresses that arriving at this place is vital, in whole or in part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Completely, or only partly' looks like a contrast of degree; the first word is the definition, the second phrase points into 'cruciAL TO GET HERe'.
explanation.definitionFit: Altogether is an adverb meaning wholly or entirely.

clue.text: A variety of exotics share the same habitat

indicators.note: a variety of suggests a varied arrangement, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Many exotic species live side by side in one environment.
explanation.definitionFit: To coexist is to live together in the same place or time without conflict.

clue.text: Occupy shortly, without husband

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the phrase for shortly goes around the husband

parts.note: shortly means soon, in a bit
H is the abbreviation for husband in genealogy and records

explanation.surface: Someone will move in soon, but alone, without a spouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking', but here it means outside: IN A BIT wraps round H.
explanation.definitionFit: To inhabit a place is to live in it, to occupy it as a home.

clue.text: Lo, nation's hero at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Behold the country's great naval hero, out on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue both describes the man and, rearranged, spells him.
explanation.definitionFit: Horatio Nelson was the British admiral who won the Battle of Trafalgar, a national naval hero.

clue.text: Creative discussions note origin of heavy fall in German capital

parts.note: B is a musical note
a rainstorm is where a heavy fall of rain comes from

indicators.note: capital means the first, upper-case letter of the word German

explanation.surface: Weather news: a downpour hits Berlin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'German capital' suggests Berlin, but it is just the capital letter G of 'German'.
explanation.definitionFit: Brainstorming is group discussion that throws out ideas freely to solve a problem.

clue.text: Sounded conspicuous

definitions.meaning: first meaning: spoken or uttered aloud, as a word is

explanation.walkthrough: Two separate senses of one word: the past tense of a verb of speaking and an adjective meaning marked.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the past form of articulate a word and an adjective for something distinct or noticeable.

clue.text: Not so polite about dean, initially, as course director

indicators.note: about means going around, so the less polite word surrounds the letter

parts.note: ruder means less polite

indicators.note: initially means taking the first letter of dean

explanation.surface: A college dean is accused of being less courteous than someone who runs a course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Course director' sounds academic, but it is what steers a ship's course.
explanation.definitionFit: A rudder is the hinged blade at a boat's stern used for steering.

clue.text: One's put on before one's taken off

definitions.text: One's put on before one's taken off

parts.words: One's put on before one's taken off
parts.note: airline passengers must fasten this safety strap before the plane takes off

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like dressing and undressing; 'taken off' is really an aircraft taking off with the passenger aboard.
explanation.definitionFit: A seat belt is a safety strap fastened across a passenger in a car or aircraft.

clue.text: 17 and I set out first

parts.note: 17 across is a nobleman, and an earl is a nobleman

indicators.note: out means disordered, so the letters of set are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cross-reference: a nobleman and the speaker set off ahead of everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 17 refers to the answer at 17 across, NOBLEMAN, of which EARL is an example; 'out' mixes SET into EST.
explanation.definitionFit: Earliest means soonest or first in time.

clue.text: Count, for example, including number 1000 in British list

indicators.note: in means the thousand is placed inside the word for list

parts.note: to list is to lean to one side, as a ship does
M is the Roman numeral for 1000

explanation.surface: An aristocrat appears on an official British register at position 1000.
explanation.walkthrough: 'List' looks like a register of names; it is the nautical verb for tilting.
explanation.definitionFit: A count is a continental aristocrat, one example of a titled peer.

clue.text: Composer liable to be shy when king enters

indicators.note: enters means the king goes into the word for liable to be shy

parts.note: from the proverb 'once bitten, twice shy': someone bitten is wary
R is the abbreviation for king, from Latin rex

explanation.surface: A timid musician whenever royalty walks into the room.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'once bitten, twice shy' links the phrase to the past participle of bite.
explanation.definitionFit: Benjamin Britten was an English composer of operas such as Peter Grimes.

clue.text: Power with which wild cat makes sudden attack

parts.note: P is the physics abbreviation for power
an ounce is the snow leopard, a wild cat

explanation.surface: A wild cat uses its strength to spring at its prey.
explanation.walkthrough: An ounce here is not a weight but another name for the snow leopard.
explanation.definitionFit: To pounce is to spring suddenly to seize or attack something.

clue.text: Business group's short time in New York, missing centre

indicators.note: in means the short time is placed inside what is left of the city's name
missing centre means the middle letter of New York is lost

parts.note: the city's name written as letters
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A firm's brief stay in New York cut short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Missing centre' drops the middle letter of the city's seven, and 'in' then slots the time abbreviation into the gap.
explanation.definitionFit: A network is a group of interconnected businesses or contacts.

clue.text: It introduces alternatives, i.e. number over one

indicators.note: over in the sense of covering, so the word for number wraps around the letter for one

parts.note: ether is an anaesthetic, something that numbs: a number
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A grammar note explains a word that offers choices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' is not a figure but something that numbs; ether was an early anaesthetic.
explanation.definitionFit: Either begins a choice between two things, as in either this or that.

clue.text: Loveless marriage, say, with one bloke? That's foolish

indicators.note: love is O, the zero score in tennis, and less means it is removed

parts.note: a marriage is a union
to tell is to say
I is the Roman numeral for one
a gent, short for gentleman, is a man, a bloke

explanation.surface: A joyless marriage, plus a man in tow, is called unwise.
explanation.walkthrough: Love is O, as in a tennis score of nil, so a loveless UNION becomes UNIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Unintelligent means lacking intelligence, which is as good as foolish.

clue.text: Lose control, in a way, as small child

parts.note: a kid is a child

explanation.surface: A toddler loses control, as small children do.
explanation.definitionFit: To skid is to slide uncontrollably, a particular way a vehicle loses grip on the road.

clue.text: Firm connection with monarch in social circle

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

indicators.note: in puts the monarch inside the word for connection

parts.note: a tie is a link or connection
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A company with royal links joins an exclusive set.
explanation.walkthrough: ER is Elizabeth Regina, Queen Elizabeth's royal cipher.
explanation.definitionFit: A coterie is a small exclusive group of people sharing interests.

clue.text: Owns something soft below the knee, as this is

definitions.text: Owns something soft below the knee, as this is

parts.note: to own something is to have it: has
a sock is soft and worn below the knee

explanation.surface: Someone possesses a soft thing that sits under the kneeling knee, just as this answer does.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue builds the word and describes it: a church kneeler is soft and sits below a kneeling worshipper's knee.
explanation.definitionFit: A hassock is a firm cushion for kneeling on in church.

clue.text: Contest truth of study and its conclusion

parts.note: a den is a private room for work, a study
the last letter of study

explanation.surface: Disputing the findings of a research paper and its final section.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Study' looks like research but is a room; 'its conclusion' is the final letter of that word.
explanation.definitionFit: To deny something is to dispute or reject the claim that it is true.

clue.text: Get awfully drunk, finally, and streak — like this

definitions.text: Get awfully drunk, finally, and streak — like this

indicators.note: awfully means badly done, so the letters are scrambled
finally means the last letter of drunk

explanation.surface: Someone gets very drunk and runs about unclothed.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue makes and describes the word: a streaker runs with no clothes on.
explanation.definitionFit: Stark naked means completely unclothed, as a streaker is.
